figures.text: Fig. 1 Workflow of AMP extraction from H. illucens larvae: from bacterial injection to peptide purification. The process includes larval injection, hemolymph collection, protein precipitation, final PF recovery and in vitro tests

Workflow of AMP extraction from H. illucens larvae: from bacterial injection to peptide purification. The process includes larval injection, hemolymph collection, protein precipitation, final PF recovery and in vitro tests

Concentrations of the samples obtained via precipitation with organic solvents from hemolymph extracted from uninfected larvae or larvae infected with E. coli or M. flavus . Data are expressed as mean ± standard errors of three independent biological replicates

Fig. 2 Microdilution assay performed against different pathogenic bacterial strains using PFs obtained via precipitation with organic solvents. The graphs represent the activity of the PFs against the following strains: ( a ) enteroinvasive Escherichia coli (EIEC), ( b ) Pseudomonas aeruginosa , ( c ) Staphylococcus aureus , ( d ) Salmonella enterica serovar Typhimurium, ( e ) Streptococcus pyogenes , ( f ) Enterococcus faecalis , and ( g ) Proteus mirabilis . CTRL = PFs from uninfected larvae; E. coli = PFs from larvae infected with Escherichia coli ; M. flavus = PFs from larvae infected with Micrococcus flavus . Data are expressed as means ± standard error of three independent biological replicates (n = 3). Statistical comparisons between treatments and control were performed by one-way ANOVA followed by Bonferroni post hoc test (* p < 0.1, ** p < 0.001, *** p < 0.0001)

Results of the microdilution assay performed to determine the minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) of PFs isolated from the hemolymph of H. illucens larvae against pathogenic and antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains, as well as the opportunistic fungus Candida albicans . MIC values are expressed in µg·µL⁻ 1
